study_title_alt: Failure of Hypertension Interventions in a Large Study Population (V3)
research_question: Among adults aged 18 years and older with two consecutive elevated office blood pressure measurements (SBP >= 130 mmHg OR DBP >= 80 mmHg per ACC/AHA 2017) within a 24-month window and no prior cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, secondary hypertension, or antihypertensive exposure, does the latency from first elevated blood pressure to recorded hypertension diagnosis predict major adverse cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or all-cause death) and incident chronic kidney disease compared to a propensity-matched normotensive comparator? Secondary aims: (a) reproduce Lu 2025's reported 29 percent higher cardiovascular risk score among patients with diagnostic delay greater than 12 months; (b) characterize antihypertensive treatment trajectories; (c) describe apparent treatment-resistant hypertension class composition and renal-sympathetic-denervation eligibility; (d) measure baseline laboratory ordering frequency including CBC, CMP, lipid panel, TSH, and serum aldosterone.
primary_objective: Quantify the association between diagnostic latency in incident hypertension and downstream MACE plus incident CKD, and reproduce Lu et al. 2025's reported 29% higher cardiovascular risk score for patients with diagnostic delay > 12 months.
scientific_rationale: Diagnostic delay in hypertension is hypothesized to allow subclinical end-organ damage to accrue before treatment, raising long-term cardiovascular and renal risk. Lu et al. 2025 reported a median diagnostic delay of 16-18 months and a 29% higher cardiovascular risk score in delayed-diagnosis patients. This study reproduces that finding on the Acumenus OMOP CDM (~1M adults) and extends it with: co-equal CKD outcome; two-component latency decomposition (first-elevated to second-elevated, and second-elevated to recorded diagnosis); apparent treatment-resistant hypertension class composition; renal-sympathetic-denervation eligibility; baseline lab ordering including serum aldosterone.
hypothesis: Patients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis more than 12 months after their second consecutive elevated office BP measurement experience higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MI, ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, all-cause death) and incident chronic kidney disease compared to (a) patients with timely diagnosis and (b) a propensity-matched normotensive comparator.

pico.population: Adults aged 18+ with two consecutive elevated office BPs (SBP >= 130 OR DBP >= 80, ACC/AHA 2017) on distinct calendar days within a 24-month window; >=365 days of prior observation; no prior cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, secondary hypertension, or antihypertensive exposure.
pico.intervention: Diagnostic latency: time from the second consecutive elevated BP (index date) to first recorded HTN diagnosis, stratified by tertile cutoffs at 6 and 12 months; sensitivity at the Lu 2025 16-month cutoff.
pico.comparator: 1:1 propensity-score-matched normotensive cohort from the same source (>=3 BPs in the same 24-mo window, all SBP <= 130 AND DBP <= 80, identical exclusions). Matched on age (+/-2yr), sex, race, calendar quarter of index. Sensitivity: greedy 1:1.
pico.outcome: Co-equal primary outcomes: (1) Composite MACE = first MI, ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, HF hospitalization (inpatient visit_occurrence required), or all-cause death; (2) Incident CKD (first dx_ckd after index with no prior CKD code).
pico.time_at_risk: Index through earliest of: 5-year follow-up (primary), end of observation, death (for non-death outcomes), or last available follow-up (sensitivity). Symmetric censoring T vs C.

risk_notes: PHI/HIPAA: Acumenus OMOP CDM uses pseudonymized person_id; no MRNs or direct identifiers persisted in study outputs.
Residual confounding from EHR data quality - mitigated via empirical calibration on OHDSI negative-control outcomes.
Incomplete death capture in OMOP death table - sensitivity analysis excluding death from MACE composite.
BP measurement context (office vs ED vs inpatient) not always recorded - filter via visit_concept_id.
changes_from_v3_protocol: Q11: Baseline kidney exclusion is eGFR < 60 (measured or estimated), NOT any CKD diagnosis code. Added lab_egfr concept set (ID 193).
Q13: Cost analysis (analysis L / Goal G) PAUSED per PI request -- removed from analysis plan.

replication_subdesign.decision: Two-design plan (Option A) per PI + user 2026-05-12
replication_subdesign.primary_design: T / C / S1 / S2 / O1-MACE / O2-CKD with PI-confirmed parameters (AHA 2017 thresholds, PSM normotensive C, eGFR <60 exclusion, co-equal CKD outcome, MACE includes all-cause death + hemorrhagic stroke)

cohort_t_lu.label: T_lu - Lu 2025 replication cohort
cohort_t_lu.bp_aggregation: drop first reading per visit, average rest; same-day multi-visit averaged
cohort_t_lu.bp_setting: outpatient only (exclude inpatient, ED, surgery center)
cohort_t_lu.treatment_naive: active Rx between -180d and +30d from 2nd BP

lu_replication_subdesign.primary_outcome_lu: Antihypertensive Rx within 30d of HTN diagnosis (binary)
lu_replication_subdesign.secondary_outcome_lu_mace: Composite of inpatient/ED MI + HF + ischemic stroke (5y from diagnosis date)
lu_replication_subdesign.statistical_model: Multivariable Cox PH adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, sex, BP, comorbidities
lu_replication_subdesign.reproduction_target: HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.23-1.36] for >365d vs. pre-2nd-BP reference, p<0.001

replication_subdesign.rationale: Faithful head-to-head Lu replication needs Lu's exact methodology; our enhanced primary design uses AHA 2017 + PSM + co-equal CKD which Lu did not. Two-design lets us report both: Lu-replicated HR vs ours-observed HR side-by-side.
